evidence.estrutura: Nise da Silveira transformed psychiatric care through local clinical institutions such as occupational-therapy workshops, the Museu de Imagens do Inconsciente and Casa das Palmeiras rather than proposing a constitutional state model. Her practice favors smaller humane institutions over totalizing centralized asylums.
evidence.representacao: She was not an electoral theorist, but her therapeutic model treated psychiatric patients as persons capable of expression rather than passive objects of authority. This supports voice and participation at the institutional level, not a strong electoral score.
evidence.poder: Her defining professional stance was opposition to coercive psychiatric practices such as electroshock, lobotomy and confinement. This strongly supports limits on institutional coercion and protection of individual dignity.
evidence.imigracao: Her work does not establish a modern immigration or assimilation doctrine. Keep this axis indeterminate.
evidence.diplomacia: She engaged internationally with Jungian psychology and exhibitions abroad, but was not a foreign-policy actor. Keep diplomacy moderate.
evidence.intervencao: No military-intervention doctrine is established. Her clinical philosophy is anti-coercive, so a restrained position is more defensible than a militarist one.
evidence.economia: Her career took place largely in public psychiatric institutions and community-oriented care, supporting public provision of health services without establishing a wider socialist ownership doctrine.
evidence.controle: She favored professional public health institutions and therapeutic standards but rejected rigid top-down institutional control. This supports moderate public coordination with strong anti-bureaucratic safeguards.
evidence.comercio: No reliable trade-policy doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: Her work drew on Jung, myth and symbolic traditions but was not a program for religious government. Use secular institutional pluralism.
evidence.moral: Her humanistic treatment of psychiatric patients, rejection of dehumanizing procedures and emphasis on affection and creative expression support progressive dignity-centered social values.
evidence.tecnologia: Her opposition to lobotomy and electroshock shows strong caution toward invasive medical technology when it violates patient dignity, while she embraced therapeutic innovation in art and occupational care. Use cautious human-centered technology rather than anti-science.
